principles.statement: Treat learner return, engagement and persistence as means to learning rather than as mastery evidence or the product’s primary educational objective.
Define a useful return as a return that reaches a meaningful learning, retrieval, review or transfer action and stores evidence; an app open or streak-save alone does not qualify.
Make progress feedback primarily capability- and evidence-based so the learner can experience truthful competence rather than inflated progress from XP, minutes or content consumption.
Support learner autonomy with meaningful choices, clear rationales and controllable routines; avoid making rewards, reminders or loss threats the main reason to study.
Use competence support by selecting achievable next actions, exposing real improvement and providing actionable feedback without hiding genuine evidence gaps.
Use gamification only as a bounded support layer and evaluate its effects on learning, useful return, motivation and friction separately.
Do not use absolute public leaderboards or harsh social comparison as a default beginner mechanic; any competitive design must be opt-in and validated for competence and learning effects.
Keep participation telemetry such as DAU, sessions, streak length, XP and minutes separate from learning evidence such as independent recall, transfer and delayed retention.
If a streak is shown, label and interpret it only as continuity of useful practice, never as English level, mastery or retained knowledge.
Design missed-day handling around recovery rather than punishment: one break must not erase capability progress, and a repair or grace path should be testable where streaks are used.
Treat a learning break as a recoverable state and give returning learners the smallest meaningful next action, compressing overdue work rather than presenting an intimidating backlog.
Support self-regulation with lightweight goal setting, planning, progress monitoring and reflection when these processes improve learning decisions rather than adding administrative burden.
Make reminders learner-controlled and behaviorally falsifiable: record whether they lead to useful returns, reduce frequency when repeatedly ignored and avoid guilt-based copy as the default.
Never increase learning load merely to preserve a streak or maximize session duration; when time or effort is constrained, prefer a smaller valid retrieval/review action.
Evaluate re-engagement explicitly after short and extended breaks instead of treating absence as irreversible churn; preserve prior learning evidence and restart from current capability state.

Keep session length, reminder cadence, progress presentation, streak/grace rules, reward type, re-entry flow, goal-setting dose and the learning-versus-engagement trade-off falsifiable until EXP-018 validates them for Vietnamese adults near A0/A1.
